move.speaker: Gregory Pine
move.proposition: Christian revelation commits Catholic theism to holding that salvation and knowledge of God are genuinely available to every person through ordinary human life.
move.sourceExcerpt: that is pertinent to the conversation from sacred scripture is 1 Timothy 2:4 God desires that all be saved and come to knowledge of the truth so it seems like a a a basic Christian commitment is the availability of the Gospel the availability of a relationship with the Lord Jesus Christ to all and it's not something that's merely for the wise or the smart or the advanced or the

components.text: Whether Catholic theism itself commits God to making salvation and knowledge genuinely available to all persons.

response.rationale: The scriptural commitment contacts the theological expectation underlying hiddenness, but it does not explain why sincere seekers experience failed contact; the answer is therefore partial.

move.speaker: Alex O'Connor
